trigger: Breach of security (unauthorized access of electronic data) involving personal information of Florida residents. Here: a student's name with information on a mental or physical condition or diagnosis by a health care professional (evaluations in about 39 student folders); and portal user names with passwords that permit access to an online account (61 accounts in the stolen spreadsheet). Encrypted data is excluded unless it can be read
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and without unreasonable delay, no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred. 15 more days are available only if good cause is given in writing to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days (501.171(3)(a))
notify: Each affected individual by mail or email to the address on file; for students who are minors, counsel confirms addressing the notice to the parent. Content: date or date range, the information accessed, and how to contact the business (501.171(4)(e))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the statute's covered entity includes a sole proprietorship. Plan to the 30-day clock

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delayed for the period the agency specifies in a written request
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request

obligation: Florida no-harm determination (alternative to individual notice)
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the business reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years; copy to the Department within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Only on counsel's advice. Unlikely when portal passwords and disability information were stolen by a criminal group

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General); content per 501.171(3)(b)
applies_at_this_tier: No - at most about 100 individuals meet the personal information definition (about 265 children's files in total); recheck the count

obligation: Florida deemed compliance through a federal regulator's notice rules
trigger: Notice given under the rules of the covered entity's primary or functional federal regulator
applies_at_this_tier: No - COPPA (16 CFR Part 312) has no breach notice rule, so there is no federal notice to substitute

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time

obligation: Third-party agent notice to the business (inbound)
trigger: Breach of a system maintained by a vendor for the business (email suite, client-management SaaS, website builder, video platform)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 10 days after the vendor determines the breach or has reason to believe it occurred
notify: The business (owner-tutor); the business still owes the notices above
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - inbound duty on vendors; track in vendor assurances (POL-01 6.1)

trigger: Former students whose families have moved out of Florida
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Check the current address of every affected former student

trigger: Compromise of personal information collected online from children (portal content, recordings)
deadline: No notice deadline: Part 312 contains no breach notification requirement
notify: None required by COPPA. The incident is evidence for the FTC of whether 312.8 safeguards were reasonable; tell portal families under the Florida notice or voluntarily
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - record the incident and lessons in the 312.8(b)(5) annual evaluation

obligation: Voluntary notice to all current families
trigger: Any incident that reaches student folders
deadline: Same day as the Florida notices, after counsel review
notify: All current families, including those whose children's files did not meet the Florida definition
applies_at_this_tier: Recommended - one message from the client-management SaaS, wording reviewed by counsel
No - FERPA does not apply (no Department of Education funds; 34 CFR 99.1)

trigger: Unencrypted customer information of 500 or more consumers acquired without authorization
applies_at_this_tier: No - not a financial institution and not a Title IV participant

obligation: Title IV breach report to FSA
citation: SAIG Enrollment Agreement (per DCL GEN-15-18); FSA Cybersecurity Breach Intake
trigger: Breach at a Title IV institution
applies_at_this_tier: No - no SAIG agreement or Title IV participation

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

citation: Voluntary; OFAC advisory (Sept. 21 2021) treats timely reporting as a mitigating factor
notify: FBI through the IC3 online report

applies_at_this_tier: No - no cyber policy; the general liability policy does not cover data breach costs (quote requested, P01 R-013)

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed only: 72 hours; 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; the proposed education criteria would not cover a tutoring business

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Covered telecommunications equipment or services found while performing a federal contract
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

trigger: A covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services) found in use or delivered under a federal contract
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
